The convergence rate O(t⁻¹) for the total relative entropy H(πt|π∗)+H(π∗|πt) arises from the interplay between the exponential weighting in the update rules and the structure of the cost function. The dual suboptimality bound O(t⁻¹) reflects the convergence of the dual potentials to their optima, while the marginal entropy decay O(t⁻²) indicates faster convergence of the marginals themselves. These rates hold for a broad class of cost functions and marginals, particularly quadratic costs with subgaussian distributions. The non-asymptotic bounds avoid exponential deterioration with regularization parameter ε, unlike prior linear convergence analyses. Stability of the optimal coupling π∗ under marginal perturbations is quantified via relative entropy, ensuring robustness in practical implementations.
